sources.title: Marcel Kurpershoek, introduction to Love, Death, Fame (NYU Press, 2022), p. xx
sources.note: Publisher PDF indexed original text read on printed p. xx: Ibn Zayd, poet of Ajwad ibn Zamil, seasonal movement, al-Dahna after rain, al-Ahsa date harvest, cheetahs and falcons. Direct fetch failed. Later main subject Ibn Zahir is explicitly not substituted for earlier Jabrid poet. Alternate paperback introduction ISBN 9781479825813 is the same work.

sources.title: Saudipedia, Ahmed Bin Atwah al-Dur‘i (2025), based on Rashid bin Mohammed bin Asaker, Darah Journal (2011)
sources.note: Direct biography read: 1456 to 1541, prosperous household, elementary curriculum, Damascus study in 1475, book endowments, return to Najd and teaching at Diriyah. No claim that this privileged education was universal.

sources.title: Doris Behrens-Abouseif, Qāytbāy’s Foundation in Medina: the Madrasah, the Ribāṭ and the Dashīshah (1998), pp. 61 to 71
sources.note: Repository metadata directly read; original indexed PDF printed p. 68 checked in full for 1482 foundation, 1484 deed, eighty hostel cells, ablution fountain, small bath, wheat storerooms, living units, primary school, mill, bakery and kitchen. Direct PDF fetch failed. All examples explicitly outside atlas polygon, not evidence of identical interior services.

sources.title: A. C. S. Peacock, Melaka in the Arabic, Persian and Turkish Sources (2024), pp. 5 to 6
sources.note: Direct full scholarly PDF read; DOI 10.1080/13639811.2024.2373582. Julfar origin, association with al-Shihr, practical sailing manuals, verse probably aiding memorization, father and grandfather sailors. Coastal examples explicitly outside polygon.

proposedOverrides.name: Arabs: Arabian societies around 1500
proposedOverrides.summary: Varied Arabian societies around 1500, with eastern oasis rulers, central settlements and wider connections.

batchIdentityNotes.scope: One distinct regional-context narrative; no association with ancient arabs, Arabia, caliphates or modern Arab identities.
batchIdentityNotes.geometry: Two identical imported polygons, world-1492 and world-1500, bounds 36.524 to 58.182 E and 15.425 to 34.597 N. Hofuf, Diriyah and al-Jubaylah included; Mecca, Medina, Jeddah, Julfar, Muscat, Aden and Radaa excluded. Site positions are rounded diagnostic points.
batchIdentityNotes.chronology: No founding event in 1492 and no collective fall in 1530. Earlier 1446 settlement, 1475 mosque, and 1480s Medina endowment are openly dated background. Later craft traditions and 1926 manuscript copy are explicitly scoped. Jabrid exact foundation/death chronology varies between cited references and is not resolved by assigning the entire map to that dynasty.
